How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a pretty confusing system

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's like an auction. You get 8 points for one semester that you use for bidding on courses. If there's a course you really want, you bid more points. You can also bid 0 points to get waitlisted on a course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mails about the course registration, and also some documents explaining it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Read about the process carefully before beginning, and look at the course bidding statistics from other years to see how popular courses are, and how many points you should bid to get the course without wasting your points.
And don't worry if you don't get enough courses the first time - there are more add/drop periods, and in the end you won't be missing any credits.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is generally lower than at UCPH, but for a lot of courses you are required to participate more, as it is part of your final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty comparable.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gendered Violence and Law 
Evidence
Trial Advocacy
Racial Profiling in Policing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Trial Advocacy. If you plan on being an advocate lawyer, this is really nice training. The class is built like a courtroom, and you get to practice everything as if it was a real trial; opening statement, direct/cross examination, closing arguments. The professor is really good and nice. The class ends with a final trial that you prepare with another student.

questions.answer: I spent a lot of money on Ubers, because the bus doesn't drive at night, and I didn't live right by the center.

questions.answer: Phone plans are way more expensive. Food at the supermarket is also more expensive. Books were less expensive than expected.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you enjoy playing a sport, I'd recommend enrolling in a sports club at the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Close by: Boler Mountain (London), Toronto, Niagara Falls
Little farther: New York (only 1.5hr by plane) Montreal, Quebec City, Ottawa, Banff, Jasper, Vancouver

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live off-campus. Don't be afraid to talk to people in your classes - canadians are generally very friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be open and social
- Remember warm clothes if you're going in the spring semester (temperature can be around -15 in winter)
- Don't go too close to the geese on campus

questions.answer: I highly recommend going to Western - the campus is amazing, and you will meet so many nice people and have the best time.
